methodological_rigor.justification: The study integrates a prospective biobanking cohort (SCANDARE, NCT03017573, 88 TNBC patients, 114 samples) with BayesPrism deconvolution against a high-resolution scRNA-seq atlas; ex vivo 3D tumor-on-chip modeling with primary patient-derived ECM-myCAFs and two TNBC cell lines; time-resolved live imaging with convolutional-neural-network-based CAF segmentation and the STAMP apoptosis-mapping algorithm; scRNA-seq (9,651 cells) with functional enrichment; PamGene kinome-wide kinase activity profiling; transwell and 2D coculture validation with Western blot; siRNA-mediated G0S2 silencing with functional rescue; SRC inhibition with dasatinib as orthogonal pharmacologic validation; and FAP− SMA+ CAP fibroblast negative control. Statistical reporting uses Shapiro–Wilk for normality and appropriate parametric/nonparametric tests; multiplicity is not globally controlled but enrichment analyses use adjusted P values. Limitations include restricted TNBC cell line diversity (2 lines), absence of in vivo model validation, and heterogeneous ECM-myCAF drug sensitivity across donors.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work identifies a clinically actionable axis: ECM-myCAF abundance at baseline and post-chemotherapy predicts chemoresistance in TNBC, and SRC inhibition by dasatinib—already an approved drug for CML/ALL—completely abolishes ECM-myCAF-mediated chemoprotection in ToCs. G0S2 is proposed as a novel mechanistic target. Although not yet validated in a prospective clinical cohort, the translational runway (dasatinib + standard TNBC chemotherapy) is concrete and the hypothesis generalizable to other cancer types where ECM-myCAFs are abundant. As a prospective cohort combined with ex vivo mechanistic work, Oxford LoE maps to 4.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE applies to the observational clinical cohort component. The SCANDARE study (NCT03017573) is registered, ethics approval (CPP Ile-de-France 3) cited, inclusion criteria and patient counts described, and RCB-based chemosensitive/chemoresistant groupings defined. Cell lines are RRID-tagged with authentication and Mycoplasma testing documented. Antibody and reagent catalog numbers are comprehensive. Statistical approach is documented with explicit distribution-based test selection. Data availability: BayesPrism reference cellular atlas (Croizer 2024) and Seurat pipeline are referenced with explicit versions and parameters, but scRNA-seq data accession numbers and analysis code repositories are not visible in the provided text (several URLs are [REDACTED]).

novelty_literature.justification: The paper delivers several novel contributions: (1) identification of the ECM-myCAF population specifically (rather than CAFs globally) as the driver of chemoresistance in TNBC; (2) the 'kiss-of-life' paradigm, with early-time-point ECM-myCAF proximity predicting long-term cancer cell fate and measured by a novel CNN-based ToC image analysis; (3) first-reported mechanistic link between ECM-myCAFs, SRC family kinase activation, and G0S2 upregulation as a chemoresistance node in TNBC; (4) demonstration that dasatinib fully abrogates ECM-myCAF-mediated chemoprotection, suggesting a repositionable combination strategy. G0S2's role in anticancer therapy resistance is explicitly noted as unreported.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is exceptionally well organized with a clear narrative arc from clinical observation to mechanistic dissection to pharmacologic rescue. Figures 1–8 progress logically and include informative schematic (Fig. 8) summarizing the proposed mechanism. Methods are detailed and reproducible at the conceptual level, including equations for survival/apoptosis calculations and IOU, CNN training specifics (InceptionResNetV2, 126 annotated crops), and precise ToC parameters (cell densities, 3.5:1 ratio, collagen concentration). Discussion honestly addresses limitations and future directions.

key_strengths: Integration of a prospective clinical cohort (SCANDARE, n=88) with BayesPrism deconvolution, ex vivo tumor-on-chip, scRNA-seq, CNN-based live imaging, kinome profiling, siRNA rescue, and pharmacologic rescue in one coherent study
Novel 'kiss-of-life' paradigm showing that early ECM-myCAF proximity (0–8 h) predicts long-term cancer cell survival under chemotherapy
First mechanistic link between ECM-myCAFs, SRC family kinase activation, TF activation (IRF1, STAT3, FOSL2, FOS, CEBPB, JUN, BHLHE40, RELA), and G0S2-dependent chemoresistance in TNBC
Actionable translational proposition: dasatinib (FDA-approved) fully abrogates ECM-myCAF-induced chemoprotection in ToCs
Specificity shown via negative control (CAP/CAF-S4 fibroblasts have no chemoprotective effect)
Cancer-cell-to-CAF ratio in ToCs (3.5:1) calibrated to patient data (3.4:1 average across 114 samples)
key_concerns: Validation limited to two TNBC cell lines (MDA-MB-231, MDA-MB-436); no in vivo mouse model or patient-derived organoid validation reported
Proposed soluble ligands (HGF, FGF2) are inferred from scRNA-seq ligand-receptor expression rather than directly validated with blocking antibodies or conditioned media
G0S2 silencing abolishes ECM-myCAF protection but the direct molecular link from SRC to G0S2 transcription (via which specific TF) is not resolved experimentally
No explicit scRNA-seq data accession number or public code repository in the provided text
Dasatinib combination effect shown ex vivo only; prospective or retrospective clinical data on dasatinib + chemotherapy in TNBC not referenced
chief_reviewer.rationale: Exceptionally well-integrated multi-modal study spanning clinical cohort, ex vivo microphysiologic modeling, single-cell and kinome profiling, gene silencing, and pharmacologic rescue, with a clear translational hypothesis; appropriate tier 1 (Nature Cancer, Cancer Discovery, JCI) with minor revisions for in vivo validation and data availability.
